result:
I saved the 2025 Q3 results to `answer.json`. Running the same script on Q2 reproduced all ten reference values exactly.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest net sales | enterprise, 362,504,311 KRW |
| b. Customers with a paid order | 246 |
| c. Category with the highest net sales | sw, 359,765,547 KRW |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the largest total refunds | u39@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders | 231 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 696,425 KRW |
| h. Growth from August to September | -10.2% |

To match the Q2 reference values, I had to handle three data issues:
- **Dates are in Korean time (UTC+9).** Timestamps are stored in UTC, so I added 9 hours before checking the quarter and month. For example, an order at `2025-06-30T15:30Z` counts as July 1.
- **One customer can have several IDs.** There are 300 customer IDs but only 250 unique emails, so I counted customers (b, f, e) by email after trimming spaces and lowercasing.
- **Segment names are inconsistent.** Values like " consumer" and "Enterprise " were trimmed and lowercased before grouping.

STATUS: DONE
